missingStrategy.mostFrequent: Fill with the most common value

preprocess.emptyNext: Load a table in the data step and you can choose what to predict here.
preprocess.columnsLead: Pick one column to predict, and the columns to predict it from.

targetRule.TARGET_NOT_NUMERIC: Regression can only predict a number column.

preprocess.notEncodable: This column holds text, so your current settings leave it out of training.
preprocess.targetSingleValue: Every row has the same value here, so there is nothing to predict.
preprocess.featureSummary: {count} feature goes into training. | {count} features go into training.
preprocess.noUsableFeature: No feature goes into training at all.
preprocess.missingNote: Text columns have no mean or median, so the most common value fills them.
preprocess.scalingNote: Evens out the size of number columns. Turn it on and off to see what changes.
preprocess.encodingNote: How text values become numbers. With it off, text columns are left out.
preprocess.testSizeNote: The rest is used to train, and this share gives the score.
preprocess.stratify: Keep each value's share the same on both sides
preprocess.randomStateNote: Fixed when the project is created. The same seed always splits the same way.
preprocess.hasMissing: This column has blanks, so your current settings cannot train.
preprocess.splitOffNote: Without a split, every row is used for training and the score comes from those same rows. The score comes out higher than it really is.

train.noTuning: This model has nothing to change.

modelOmission.tooLarge: The model was too big to fit in the file. Training again will not help — try lowering a setting that makes the model bigger, such as the number of trees.
modelOmission.engineUnsupported: Models trained here cannot be saved yet, so only the scores were kept.
